commitResults.messageBody: Add Maneerat Apicha's AboutUs details
Update project website branding and links
Update DG target user, value proposition and user stories
Add Use Cases to Developer Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove AB3 contact email from About Us

commitResults.messageBody: Remove AB3 contact email from About Us

Poco Book has no dedicated value objects for guardian contact details.
The add-student feature needs validated guardian values before parser,
storage, and UI integration.

Add immutable guardian name and phone objects with normalized storage.
Preserve name capitalization for display and ignore case in equality,
with consistent hashing. Require eight phone digits starting with 6, 8,
or 9, and remove spaces and hyphens before storage.

Follow the submitted MVP rules and error messages so later integration
can rely on one validation contract. Cover invalid inputs, boundaries,
normalization, Unicode case variants, and equality with unit tests.

Validation: ./gradlew check passes all 252 tests and Checkstyle.

Refs: #25
Add guardian contact value objects
Add regression tests for find and filtered-list indexes
Align index parsing with the MVP specification

commitResults.messageTitle: Add students with guardian contact and optional fee
commitResults.messageBody:
The add command still required AB3's phone, email and address, and
had no way to record a guardian or an outstanding fee, so tutors could
not record a student as specified in Feature 1 of the MVP spec.

Let's require n/, g/ and gp/, make p/, e/, a/ and f/ optional, and
validate every field with the spec's rules and exact messages.
Duplicates are now the same name, ignoring case and extra spaces, with
the same guardian phone. Guardian details and the fee are saved and
loaded so they survive a restart.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep the selected student's details current
commitResults.messageBody:
Editing the viewed student with edit or setoutstanding cleared the
details pane, although the User Guide says the selection stays while
the student is still displayed. The list panel looked for the old
Person, which an edit replaces.

The list panel now records in-place replacements and restores the
edited student. The details pane also shows the fee as S$AMOUNT, as
the cards and command results do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Align edit output with the User Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
edit reported an invalid index as "The person index provided is
invalid." instead of the student message the User Guide specifies,
and still used AB3's "person" wording. Command results also no
longer listed tags, so a successful tag edit showed no change.

edit also absorbed g/, gp/ and f/ into the preceding value, so
"edit 1 a/123 Street g/New Guardian" saved that text as the address.
These fields cannot be edited, so edit now rejects them with the
invalid-command-format message.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow prefix-like text in add addresses
commitResults.messageBody:
add rejected addresses such as "c/o Mr Lim" or "Blk A/B" as unknown
prefixes, although Address allows '/' and edit accepts them. Only
values other than the address are now checked for unknown prefixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept find keywords that have no letters
commitResults.messageBody:
find validated each keyword as a full name, which needs a letter, so
"find Alex 2" failed although "Alex 2" is a valid name. Keywords are
now checked against the name characters only, and are normalized to
NFC like stored names.

list, find, fees, help and exit saved the address book. If the data
file failed to load, any of them overwrote it with an empty book.
Like view, they no longer save.

Also replace list's AB3 "Listed all persons." with "Listed all
students.".

commitResults.messageTitle: Report oversized setoutstanding index as invalid
commitResults.messageBody:
An index above 2147483647 gave an invalid-command-format message,
unlike delete, edit and view, which report "The student index
provided is invalid.". setoutstanding now uses the same index parsing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null entries in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A null entry in the persons list caused an uncaught
NullPointerException on startup. It is now reported as invalid data,
so the app starts with an empty address book as for other invalid
files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the guides for the v1.3 fixes
commitResults.messageBody:
The Quick Start and manual-testing add examples omitted the required
g/ and gp/ parameters, so pasting them failed. Update them, and
document the behaviour changed by the preceding fixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject null tag entries in the data file
commitResults.messageBody:
A null entry in a student's tags list caused an uncaught
NullPointerException on startup. Report it as an invalid tag so the app
starts with an empty address book as for other invalid files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show guardian contact details on student cards
commitResults.messageBody:
Student cards omitted guardian name and phone, so two students with the
same name and no optional student contact details appeared identical in
the list, contradicting UC02 extension 2b.

Display each student's guardian name and phone on their card.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update version, help URL, and guide details
commitResults.messageBody:
Point HelpWindow.USERGUIDE_URL to the Poco Book User Guide, bump
MainApp.VERSION to V1.3.0, add exit to the User Guide command summary,
and document guardian card labels under list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Start edit and delete details on a new line
commitResults.messageBody:
Messages.format returns a multi-line student summary starting with
"Name: ...". AddCommand separates its header from this block with a
newline, whereas EditCommand and DeleteCommand placed "Name: ..." on
the same line as "Edited student:" or "Deleted student:".

Place a newline after "Edited student:" and "Deleted student:" so all
formatted student fields align consistently on their own lines.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match default window width to minimum width
commitResults.messageBody:
MainWindow.fxml and the Developer Guide specify a minimum window width
of 750 px, whereas GuiSettings.DEFAULT_WIDTH was still 740 px.

Update GuiSettings.DEFAULT_WIDTH to 750 so fresh launches and saved
default preferences match the minimum window width.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject broken external symlinks in runtime paths
commitResults.messageBody:
ApplicationPaths.resolveWithin called Path.toRealPath() on existing
directory entries without following links first. When a runtime path
component was a dangling symbolic link, toRealPath() threw
NoSuchFileException and wrapped it in IllegalStateException instead of
checking whether the link target stayed inside the home folder. In
addition, MainApp resolved its runtime paths in static field
initializers, so an invalid link caused ExceptionInInitializerError
whenever MainApp was loaded.

Inspect symbolic link targets when the destination does not exist yet so
broken links escaping the home folder raise IllegalArgumentException,
and defer MainApp runtime path resolution to init().

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow edit command to update guardian details
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand and EditCommandParser reject the guardian name (g/) and
guardian phone (gp/) prefixes, so tutors cannot update guardian contact
details without deleting and re-adding a student.

Allow users to update a student's guardian name and guardian phone
through the edit command while keeping untouched fields and duplicate
student identity checks intact.

Closes #107

commitResults.messageTitle: Add logging to EditCommand and EditCommandParser
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand and EditCommandParser lack feature-level diagnostic logs
for parsed edit descriptors and completed student updates.

Log parsed edit descriptors at FINE in EditCommandParser and successful
student edits at INFO in EditCommand using LogsCenter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document guardian edit in Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide does not yet describe how the edit command updates
guardian details or verifies student identity after an edit.

Add an Implementation section and sequence diagram explaining how
EditCommandParser and EditCommand update guardian fields while
preserving untouched fields and checking duplicate student identity.

commitResults.messageTitle: Expand guardian edit tests and builder support
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand.MESSAGE_USAGE omits a guardian prefix in its example, and
EditPersonDescriptorBuilder does not support guardian fields directly,
requiring manual setter calls in tests. Test coverage also combines
single-field guardian edits and lacks dedicated checks for shared
guardian phones, gp/-only identity collisions, and filtered persistence.

Include gp/ in EditCommand's usage example and add guardian support to
EditPersonDescriptorBuilder and PersonUtil. Split the single-field
guardian edit tests and add regression tests for shared guardian phones,
gp/-only duplicate identity checks, and filtered edits persisted through
LogicManager and JsonAddressBookStorage.
Allow edit command to update guardian details

The add command does not accept t/, so tutors must run edit after
every add to tag a student. A t/ typed after a/ is also exempt from
the unknown-prefix check and is silently stored as address text.

Accept repeatable t/TAG in add, parsing it with ParserUtil#parseTags
so tags no longer leak into the address. Update the add usage text,
User Guide and parser tests.

Fixes #182.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore edge punctuation when finding names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names may end in or be wrapped by punctuation, such as "Wei Ming Tan."
or "Ali (Junior)", but find compared whole words including that
punctuation, so searching by surname missed these students.

Let's also match words after removing punctuation at their start and
end, keeping punctuation inside a word so only full words match.

Fixes #192

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain the rule when rejecting a duplicate student
commitResults.messageBody:
Adding or editing a student into a duplicate only reported "This
student already exists", so the tutor had to guess which field to
change.

Let's state that another student has the same name and guardian phone,
and suggest changing either to tell them apart.

Fixes #195

commitResults.messageTitle: Name every missing required parameter in add
commitResults.messageBody:
"add n/Fred" reported only the missing g/, so after supplying it the
tutor hit a second error for gp/.

Let's list all missing required prefixes in one error.

Fixes #196

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the problem when rejecting fees arguments
commitResults.messageBody:
"fees min/abc" and "fees x/5" both reported only "Invalid command
format!", unlike setoutstanding, which names the invalid amount.

Let's report whether the minimum amount is missing, invalid or repeated,
or which unexpected text was given.

Fixes #197

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject an edit that changes nothing
commitResults.messageBody:
"edit 1 n/Alex Yeoh" on a student already named Alex Yeoh reported
"Edited student" and rewrote the data file, implying a change was made.

Let's reject such an edit with a message saying nothing changed.

The test for sharing a guardian phone edited a student to the phone it
already had, so it now gives that student a different phone first.

Fixes #198

commitResults.messageTitle: Grow the result display to fit command feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
The result area is fixed at 100 px, so add and edit confirmations
show only the first three lines; the guardian and outstanding fee
lines must be scrolled to, and enlarging the window does not help.

Let the result area take its height from the result display, and set
the text area's row count from the feedback's line count, between 3
rows (the old height) and 10 rows. Longer feedback such as help text
still scrolls, so the student list stays visible.

Fixes #181.

commitResults.messageTitle: Name the failing field in validation errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Student and guardian fields share the same constraint messages, so an
invalid g/ or gp/ value is reported as if n/ or p/ were wrong. edit
1 f/50 only prints the usage, which does not mention f/, and edit
1 n/Alex x/foo blames the name rule for a mistyped prefix.

Give GuardianName and GuardianPhone their own messages, reject f/ in
edit with a pointer to setoutstanding and paid, and apply add's
unknown-prefix check to edit. Move the prefix-like token check into
ParserUtil so both parsers share it.

Fixes #188.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Poco Book wording in clear and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
The clear and exit commands still reply with AB3 wording ("Address
book has been cleared!", "Exiting Address Book ..."), and five User
Guide sentences call the student list an address book.

Name Poco Book in both command messages and the User Guide, and add
tests that pin the new messages.

Fixes #183.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow S/O and D/O in student and guardian names
commitResults.messageBody:
Names such as "Ravi S/O Raj" are rejected: add reports a generic
format error because S/ looks like a prefix, and edit reports the name
rules, which do not allow slashes.

Accept S/O and D/O, in any case, as separate words in student and
guardian names, and exempt them from the prefix-like token check. All
other slashes in names are still rejected. Mention the rule in the
constraint messages and the User Guide.

Fixes #162.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the supported name and email characters
commitResults.messageBody:
Curly apostrophes and Unicode dashes in names, and apostrophes in
emails, are rejected with messages that seem to allow them, and
neither find nor the duplicate check matches ß with SS. These inputs
are rare for our target users, so we keep the current rules rather
than widen validation and matching.

State the exact supported characters in the name and email
constraint messages, and describe the limits in the User Guide's add
and find sections and Known issues.

Fixes #156, fixes #161, fixes #165.

commitResults.messageTitle: Let edit clear optional contact fields
commitResults.messageBody:
A student can be added without a phone, email or address, but once
set, edit cannot remove them: an empty p/, e/ or a/ is rejected, so a
tutor must keep a wrong value or delete and re-add the student.

Treat an empty p/, e/ or a/ in edit as removing that field. Track the
removal separately in EditPersonDescriptor so that omitting a prefix
still keeps the old value. Guardian fields stay required. Document
the syntax in the usage text and User Guide.

Fixes #151.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the name, address and email limits for add
commitResults.messageBody:
The add section described the phone and fee rules but not the
name, guardian name, address and email limits, so tutors found them
only when an input was rejected.

Let's state each limit, counted as the app counts it, with accepted and
rejected examples.

Fixes #158

commitResults.messageTitle: Say which commands ignore extra text
commitResults.messageBody:
The command-format notes said that commands taking no parameters ignore
extra text, but feesummary rejects "feesummary 1". They also said that
parameters can be in any order, but "setoutstanding 75.50 1" is
rejected.

Let's name the commands that ignore extra text, and limit the
any-order rule to parameters with a prefix.

Fixes #160

commitResults.messageTitle: Refresh the details pane after every command
commitResults.messageBody:
After a capitalisation-only edit such as `edit 1 g/adrian yeoh`, the
new record equals the old one, because guardian names compare without
case. The selection listener only fires when the selected item changes
by equals, so the details pane kept showing the old name.

Read the selected record from the list by index, and refresh the
details pane from it after every successful command instead of relying
on the listener alone.

Phones, WhatsApp and contact cards show Singapore numbers as
+65 9123 4567, so a tutor pasting a guardian's number got a validation
error from add and edit, and an invalid-format error from findguardian.

Accept an optional +65 before the 8 digits in Phone and GuardianPhone,
and remove it when storing, so +65 9123 4567 is stored as 91234567.
Let findguardian accept a +65 phone keyword. Other country codes are
still rejected.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the result display row count without JavaFX
commitResults.messageBody:
UI tests run only with POCO_UI_TESTS, so CI never ran the new row
count logic and the codecov patch check failed. Move the calculation
into ResultDisplay#rowCountFor and test it directly.

commitResults.messageTitle: Compare validation messages with their constants in tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The fee-prefix test copied MESSAGE_FEE_NOT_EDITABLE as a literal, and the
guardian-name test pinned the whole message. Assert against the
constant, and check only that the guardian message names its field.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check the product name instead of repeating the message in tests
commitResults.messageBody:
The clear and exit message tests compared each constant with a copy of
itself, so they could not catch a regression. Check that each message
names Poco Book and no longer says Address Book.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a name that is only S/O or D/O, and share name validation
commitResults.messageBody:
S/O was replaced with SO before the letter check, so a name of just S/O
was accepted. Require a letter outside the markers.

GuardianName repeated Name's whole validation chain. Delegate to Name so
the two cannot drift apart.

# Conflicts:
#	src/main/java/seedu/address/model/person/GuardianName.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Say again that emails cannot contain spaces
commitResults.messageBody:
The rewritten message dropped the no-spaces rule, so student @example.com
got a message that never mentioned the space.

# Conflicts:
#	src/test/java/seedu/address/model/person/GuardianNameTest.java

# Conflicts:
#	src/test/java/seedu/address/model/person/GuardianNameTest.java

commitResults.messageTitle: Report stray prefixes after t/ and empty tags in add
Say ASCII letters in the email constraint
Pin the clear and exit messages in tests
Say unprefixed parameters come before prefixed ones
Build the fees range message from the maximum amount
Refresh the details pane after a failed command
Share phone validation between Phone and GuardianPhone
Document guardian-edit rules and add manual tests
Use full sentences in StringUtil parameter docs
Derive edit prefix validation from accepted prefixes
Clarify name syntax and share the edit prefix list
Reject marker-only names and share the edit prefix list
Distinguish fees validation causes in diagnostic logs
Pin the guardian phone constraint wording
Treat tags differing only in case as one tag
commitResults.messageBody:
Tags were compared case-sensitively, so "edit 1 t/Math t/math" stored
two tags with the same meaning on the student card.

Let's compare tags without regard to case. When the same tag is given
twice in different cases, the first one typed is kept.

Fixes #193

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain why t/ cannot be combined with other tags
commitResults.messageBody:
"edit 1 t/ t/x" was rejected with "Tag names should be alphanumeric",
although both t/ and t/x are valid on their own, so the message pointed
the user at the wrong problem.

Let's report that t/ clears all tags and so cannot be combined with
other tags.

Fixes #194

commitResults.messageTitle: Give a separate error for a repeated t/ in edit
commitResults.messageBody:
edit 1 t/ t/ said t/ cannot be combined with other tags, but no other
tag was given. Say that t/ should be given only once instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Cover and document legacy case-variant tags
Name students left on the old guardian phone after an edit
commitResults.messageBody:
Siblings share a guardian, but edit changes one student at a time.
After changing one sibling's guardian phone, nothing told the tutor
that the others were still on the old number, so a later findguardian
by the new number missed them.

When edit changes the guardian phone, list the other students who still
have the old phone in the feedback. The edit itself is unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop the redundant identity check in the shared-phone note
Use grammatical shared-phone feedback and precise fixture comments
Require S/O and D/O between names, and share the marker pattern

Add Zhao Shizhen's AboutUs details
Add Suvan Handa's AboutUs details
Add EL-NAIT's profile photo
Update EL-NAIT's AboutUs details

commitResults.messageTitle: Update DG target user, value proposition and user stories
Add more details to developer guide
Add regression tests for find and filtered-list indexes
commitResults.messageBody:
Find matching rules and index resolution after a find had little
test coverage, so later MVP changes could break them unnoticed.

Let's add FindCommandTest cases for single, multiple, case-insensitive,
partial-word, zero-match and result-order behaviour, plus an
integration test showing that delete after find uses the index in the
filtered list.

No production change is needed; current behaviour meets the spec.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use student wording in find and delete messages
commitResults.messageBody:
The app manages students, but find and delete still reported results
in terms of 'persons', which does not match the product or issue #3's
requirement that find states the number of students listed.

Let's update the result, error and usage messages for find and delete,
and reuse the existing student index error message (as view does).
Constant names are kept so existing references stay valid.

commitResults.messageTitle: Decouple find integration test from index error wording
commitResults.messageBody:
PR #67 changes delete's invalid-index error from the person message to
the student message. Asserting the exact text here would make this test
fail whichever of the two PRs merges second.

Let's assert only the exception type and that no data changed, leaving
the exact error text to DeleteCommandTest.
Use student wording in find and delete messages

commitResults.messageTitle: Show guardian and fee details in delete success message
commitResults.messageBody: The delete success message only shows the original AB3 fields, so tutors cannot see the guardian contact or outstanding fee of the student they just removed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject find keywords that cannot appear in a name
commitResults.messageBody:
find accepts any keyword, so `find @@@` succeeds with an empty list
and clears what the tutor was looking at, although no student name
can ever contain such a word. It also has no test that guardian
names are excluded from the search.

Let's reject keywords that fail the existing name rule, keeping the
displayed list unchanged, and add a test that a keyword matching
only the guardian name finds nothing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use S$ for fees in student details and test delete after fees
commitResults.messageBody:
The delete success message shows fees with a `$` prefix, while the
MVP spec, the student card and the fee commands all use `S$`. Also,
#2 requires delete to use the index of the list shown by `fees`, but
nothing tested this because `fees` was not merged yet.

Let's use `S$` in the formatted student details, and add a test that
deletes the third student in the `fees` list, which is a different
student from the third one in the full list.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document find keyword rules and drop redundant comment
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide does not say that find rejects keywords which cannot
appear in a name, or that guardian, contact and fee details are not
searched. The comment above the keyword check also just repeats what
the code says.

Let's add both points to the find section of the user guide and
remove the comment.
Show guardian and fee details in delete success message
Reject find keywords that cannot appear in a name

Tutors need to find a student when they only remember the guardian's
name or phone number.

Match any keyword against whole guardian-name words, ignoring case, or
against the exact stored 8-digit guardian phone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Match guardian phone keywords typed with separators
commitResults.messageBody:
add and edit accept gp/9234-5678 and store 92345678, so a tutor
searching the way they typed it found nobody.

Normalize phone-shaped keywords with GuardianPhone before comparing.
Also copy the keyword list, reject null arguments, add hashCode and
document the constructor, with tests for compound names, numeric name
words and the defensive copy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add findguardian command to search by guardian name or phone
commitResults.messageBody:
Tutors often remember a guardian's name or number from a message
rather than the student's name, but find only searches student names.

Add FindGuardianCommand and its parser. Keywords use the guardian-name
character rules, search all stored students regardless of the current
filter, and leave stored data unchanged.

Command registration and user guide text are left to the shared
integration PR, as agreed in #98.

commitResults.messageTitle: Harden findguardian parser and command from review
commitResults.messageBody:
Reject null arguments in the command and parser, mark parse with
@Override, fix its Javadoc tags, and say in the usage text which phone
numbers are matched.

Add tests that go through the parser for a hyphenated phone and for
siblings sharing a guardian, checking each sibling is listed once in
stored order even after a prior filter.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add guardian search sequence diagram to the Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG explains every v1.4 feature except findguardian, so developers
cannot see how a guardian search flows from parsing to filtering.

Add a sequence diagram of findguardian mei 9234-5678 and a Guardian
search section covering parsing, matching rules, the read-only save
behavior and the main design decisions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Clarify guardian search diagram and keyword rules from review
commitResults.messageBody:
Label r as the CommandResult in the sequence diagram, and list the
characters a findguardian keyword may contain so readers can see why
phone keywords such as 9234-5678 pass validation.
Add guardian search sequence diagram to the Developer Guide

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore command box input that is only whitespace
commitResults.messageBody:
Pressing Enter on a command box holding only spaces passed the input
to the parser. The parser rejected it as an invalid command format and
showed the help usage, although the tutor never typed help.

Let's treat blank input like empty input, so nothing is executed and
the command box keeps its normal style.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject a JSON data file that holds only null
commitResults.messageBody:
A data or preferences file containing just "null" deserialized to a
null object. Optional.of then threw a NullPointerException, so the app
exited before showing its window.

Let's report such a file as a DataLoadingException, like any other
invalid file. Startup then falls back to an empty address book or to
default preferences, as the UG promises for invalid data.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use tutor-relevant tags in the sample data
commitResults.messageBody:
A fresh launch showed the sample students tagged friends, colleagues,
neighbours, family and classmates, carried over from AB3. Those tags
mean nothing to a tutor and suggest the data was never adapted.

Let's tag the sample students with levels and subjects instead, such
as Sec3, JC1, Math and Physics. Names, guardians and fees are kept, so
the manual test instructions that rely on them still hold.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the policy for unknown fields in data files
commitResults.messageBody:
Unknown fields in addressbook.json and preferences.json are ignored on
reading, because Jackson is configured not to fail on them. Poco Book
writes only the fields it knows, so the next save drops them silently.
Nothing recorded whether this was intended.

Let's keep the current behaviour, record the decision and its
alternatives in the DG, and tell users in the UG that unrecognised
fields are not kept. A storage test pins down that such fields are
ignored on reading and dropped on saving.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document separators, address prefixes and filter resets
commitResults.messageBody:
Three command-entry behaviours were undocumented:

* Pasted tabs are removed by the command box, and non-breaking spaces
  are not separators, so such commands are rejected unexpectedly.
* A mistyped prefix after a/, such as GP/, is silently stored as part
  of the address instead of updating that field.
* add and edit reset the displayed list to all students, while
  setoutstanding and paid keep the filter. Only edit said so.

Let's keep these behaviours, which reject bad input without changing
data and keep free-form addresses such as c/o working, and document
them in the UG. The DG records why add and edit reset the filter.
Update Suvan Handa's project responsibilities

commitResults.messageTitle: Update project website branding and links
Persist guardian and outstanding fee data
commitResults.messageBody:
Student records do not retain guardian contacts or optional fees through
application restarts, preventing dependent features from relying on stored
data.

Let's extend the model and JSON adapter with validated guardian and fee
fields. Add round-trip and invalid-data coverage so normalized phones, fee
boundaries, absent fees, ordering, and duplicate behavior remain stable.

Person now hashes guardian and outstanding-fee fields, but the updated
hashCode path is not exercised.

Let's verify equal records produce the same hash code so the equality
contract remains covered as fields evolve.
Make absent outstanding fees explicit through Optional and update callers to handle them safely. Use realistic sample fees and clarify why edit tests preserve fields that edit cannot change.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add automated AI pull request reviews
commitResults.messageBody:
Provide non-blocking PR feedback through the configured LLM endpoint.
Use the trusted base commit so fork code never runs with secrets.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace single-request AI review with sandbox-tested PR-Agent batching

commitResults.messageBody: Replace AI review script with tested batched PR-Agent reviews

The fees command lists every student with an outstanding fee, so tutors
cannot focus the list on students owing at least a chosen amount.

Add an optional min/AMOUNT threshold while preserving plain fees and the
existing result-count message. Keep the query read-only and reject invalid
arguments without changing the displayed list or stored records.

Cover amount boundaries, strict parsing, search replacement, displayed
indexes, fee clearing, and the storage boundary with fees-specific tests.

Implements #119.

commitResults.messageTitle: Address minimum fee filtering review feedback
commitResults.messageBody:
Numeric threshold equality lacks a matching hash code, and the live
filter tests only cover clearing a fee entirely.

Normalize threshold hashes and test positive fees crossing the minimum
to protect value equality and inclusive live filtering. Reuse the shared
amount regex and plain-fee predicate to avoid duplicated definitions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add logging for minimum fee filtering
commitResults.messageBody:
Fee filtering lacks feature-level diagnostics for successful queries
and rejected arguments.

Log the threshold and result count at INFO and parser diagnostics at
FINE using LogsCenter, consistent with existing logging conventions.
Avoid including student records in these messages.

Direct command callers can supply negative thresholds, and command
diagnostics omit the minimum amount.

Reject negative constructor inputs, describe thresholds with
ToStringBuilder, and make the parser null precondition explicit.
Add regression tests and rename the integration test to describe its
inclusive filtering and no-save guarantees.

Explain the minimum-fee query so future developers can follow its
parsing, live filtering and no-save behavior. Add a sequence diagram
and its rendered image beside the implementation explanation.

Relates to #100; documents the implementation in #137.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions for Gradle run task

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct manual tests and guide instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
The launch and migration instructions assume behavior that a fresh app does not provide, and the guardian-search walkthrough contains rejected placeholders and unspecified amounts. This makes the documented checks hard to reproduce.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain unsupported money notation in fee inputs
commitResults.messageBody:
Fee commands reject currency-formatted amounts with a range error even
when the numerical value is valid. That response does not tell tutors
how to enter the same amount successfully.

Keep the documented plain-number syntax and storage validation intact.
Identify currency symbols, commas, and redundant f/ prefixes before
range validation in add and setoutstanding, and explain the supported
input in their feedback and the User Guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fit deletion dialog within small screens
commitResults.messageBody:
The delete-confirmation dialog grows beyond the documented usable
height when both names reach their supported limits and a fee warning
is present. The opt-in Windows UI regression fails before this change.

Give long fields more horizontal room, reduce the gap between content
blocks, and trim the warning banner padding. Keep the warning, full
names, instructions, and Y/N confirmation behavior visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document the supported tag character set
commitResults.messageBody:
Names accept multilingual characters, but subject tags use an ASCII
alphanumeric validator. The guide does not explain this difference,
so tutors cannot tell which subject labels are supported.

State the accepted tag characters and give accepted and rejected
examples without widening the input contract during the ongoing tag
normalization work.

Two app instances keep independent in-memory books while saving to
the same file. A stale instance can overwrite records saved by a
newer one, even when their commands run at different times.

Limit supported usage to one instance per home folder, and warn users
at startup and in the FAQ. Explain the storage reason in the DG so
the restriction is discoverable to maintainers as well as tutors.

Clear immediately removes every stored student, including hidden
records and unpaid fees, without confirmation or undo. The guide
states the command but does not tell tutors how to avoid accidental
loss when they intend to keep a recoverable copy.

Warn at the command instructions and describe a manual backup. Record
that a confirmation workflow needs separate design and regression
work, and distinguish successful clear from failed-save protection.

The User Guide illustrates the help window with an AB3 URL even though
Poco Book opens its own guide. A reader copying the displayed URL
would reach the wrong application.

Capture the current HelpWindow content rendered by JavaFX on Windows
and replace the old image. Explain that the image omits the operating
system's frame so it is not mistaken for a full-window capture.

Preferences may contain nonpositive or nonfinite window dimensions,
or coordinates from a monitor that has been disconnected. Passing
those settings directly to JavaFX can leave the window unusable.

Use default dimensions for invalid values and recenter a window whose
title area is not on any connected screen. Preserve valid geometry,
cover the actual Stage behavior in opt-in UI tests, and update the
User and Developer Guides to match the new recovery behavior.

Maximum-length contact fields can wrap beyond the visible details
pane at the minimum window size. Existing tests check the displayed
text but do not check that the final fields remain reachable.

Exercise a narrow, short live JavaFX details pane with valid boundary
values. Scroll to the bottom and check that the final tags field is
visible, retaining the need for a full main-window manual inspection.

The Model diagram routes the all-student and filtered-student
associations into Person at the same point. At the DG embed width,
the role labels overprint and are hard to distinguish.

Route the two associations from distinct directions and regenerate
the PNG while keeping their endpoints and multiplicities. Link the
embedded image to its full-resolution version for closer inspection.

Add guidance for invalid commands and ignore command casing
commitResults.messageBody:
Command words must be typed in lower case. `List`, `Help` and `lsit`
all show only `Unknown command.`, and `help lsit` repeats the whole
`help` usage under `Invalid command format!`. A tutor who has Caps Lock
on, or who mistypes a command word, gets no hint about what went wrong
or which command words exist.

Let's,
* match command words and `help` targets in any letter case
* name the unknown word, point to `help COMMAND` and list the available
  command words
* give `help` with an unknown word or extra words a short error instead
  of the whole `help` usage
* keep prefixes such as `n/` case-sensitive, so `N/A` in an address is
  not split into a name
* reword the `help` usage to say what `help COMMAND` does

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject trailing JSON content and duplicate keys
commitResults.messageBody:
A hand-edited data file with content after its first JSON value, or
with a field name repeated in one object, loaded only in part. The
next save then dropped the ignored content without any sign.

Treat such files as invalid, like any other invalid file, so Poco Book
starts empty and keeps the file until a data-changing command. Jackson
2.7.4 has no FAIL_ON_TRAILING_TOKENS, so JsonUtil checks for the end of
input itself.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain that a change whose save failed is saved later
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG use cases for add, delete, setoutstanding and paid said that a
change whose save failed is kept only until Poco Book is closed. But
the change stays in the model, and the next successful save writes
the whole address book, so a later change also saves it. The UG said
a payment survives a restart unless a save error is reported.

Let's describe this in the four use cases and the UG, add a manual
test that saves a failed change with a later one, and add a
LogicManager test that keeps this behaviour from changing silently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Explain why the JavaFX toolkit cannot be reused in UI tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Each JavaFX UI test class started the toolkit and ignored the
IllegalStateException that JavaFX throws once a start has begun,
assuming that another test had started it. If that toolkit had shut
down, Platform.runLater dropped every task, and if its start had
failed, runLater blocked forever. The tests then timed out or hung
with no hint of why.

Let's start the toolkit through one test helper that checks, with a
bounded wait, that a reused toolkit still runs tasks, and otherwise
fails with a message and the original error as its cause. The helper
also keeps the toolkit running after a test closes its last window.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageBody:

Let's state that an existing file keeps its permissions, that a new
preferences.json is owner-only, and that a new data/addressbook.json
still gets the default permissions because JsonAddressBookStorage
creates the empty file first.

commitResults.messageBody:

commitResults.messageTitle: Let setoutstanding add to an outstanding fee with a +AMOUNT form
commitResults.messageBody:
There was no way to charge a student again before the earlier amount was
settled: the tutor had to work out the new total and retype it, which is slow
and can silently drop the earlier charge.

setoutstanding INDEX +AMOUNT now adds to the fee already recorded:
- parser accepts the + prefix, rejects +0 and anything outside 0.01-99999.99;
- execute adds to the current amount (absent fee counts as 0.00), and refuses a
  total above S$99999.99 with a message naming the refused amount and the total;
- feedback shows the transition, e.g. "Added S$50.00 ... S$120.00 -> S$170.00";
- help setoutstanding, the user guide, UC06 and the manual tests are updated.

Replacement and clearing keep their existing behaviour and messages.

Fixes #228.

commitResults.messageTitle: Recover from a null guiSettings in preferences.json instead of crashing at startup

A preferences.json containing "guiSettings": null loaded into a UserPrefs whose
nested settings were null, and the copy into ModelManager threw a
NullPointerException before the window appeared. Startup could not be recovered
without deleting the file by hand.

- UserPrefs(ReadOnlyUserPrefs) falls back to the default GuiSettings when the
  source reports null; the strict setGuiSettings(null) contract is unchanged.
- JsonUserPrefsStorage#readUserPrefs normalises through that constructor, so
  MainApp#initPrefs saves a repaired file and the next launch is clean.
- Regression tests fail on the previous code and pass now.

Fixes #170.

commitResults.messageTitle: Accept capitalisation-only guardian and tag edits
commitResults.messageBody:
EditCommand rejected an edit as a no-op when the edited student was
equal to the current one. Guardian names and tags compare without
regard to case, so `edit 1 g/adrian yeoh` on a guardian saved as
`Adrian Yeoh` was refused with "No changes made", and the tutor could
not fix the capitalisation.

Compare the exact text of every field instead, through a new
Person#hasIdenticalDetails. Equality for duplicate detection and
search is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Start student card content at the top of the card
commitResults.messageBody:
Student cards have a minimum height and centred their content
vertically. A student with only a name and a guardian contact therefore
showed an empty gap above the name, which looked like a rendering
fault.

Align the card content to the top-left so every card starts its name at
the same place.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Count wrapped rows when sizing the result display
commitResults.messageBody:
The result display chose its height from the number of line breaks in
the feedback. A long line that wraps, such as the add usage shown after
`add n/Fred`, took more rows than counted, so the end of the message
was hidden behind a scroll bar.

Measure how many rows each line wraps to at the display's current
width, and recompute when the width changes. Before layout, each line
still counts as one row.
